articleOfWeek.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articleOfWeek.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articleOfWeek.abstract: Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. Purpose We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). Methods We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. Results We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99 th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Conclusion Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Principles of drug dosing for obese patients in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of severe obesity in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has led to several challenges with medication dosing. Doses listed in product labels or tertiary references typically do not account for the pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic variability encountered with obesity, leading to the potential for treatment failure or an adverse effect. The purpose of this review is to provide guidance for ICU clinicians when crafting pharmacotherapy regimens in critically ill patients with extreme obesity. A literature search was performed to identify relevant articles pertaining to the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of medications in obese patients. Articles describing both general treatment principles and medication specific assessments were retrieved. Bibliographies were searched for additional publications. Evidence guiding medication use in critically ill obese patients is limited by the small number of patients with more extreme forms of obesity, the lack of clinical outcome measurements, and the few studies that are specific to the ICU. Obesity-related alterations in pharmacokinetic parameters, such as apparent volume of distribution and drug clearance, may hinder attainment of pharmacodynamic targets. Individualized dosing strategies are essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review provides dosing recommendations for selected ICU medications and proposes a practical framework to guide medication dosing decisions in this patient population. Drug dosing in critically ill obese patients should be individualized by assessing pharmacokinetic variability and whether pharmacodynamic goals can be achieved. Selecting the correct weight for weight-based calculations or dose for fixed regimens is paramount for achieving these goals. Consultation with a clinical pharmacist may be beneficial.

articles.title: Subcutaneous insulin for mild-to-moderate diabetic ketoacidosis: a scoping review and implementation framework.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common emergency department (ED) presentation associated with high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization. While intravenous (IV) insulin remains the most common treatment, emerging data suggest subcutaneous (SUBQ) insulin may be a feasible alternative for patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. This scoping review summarizes current evidence of SUBQ insulin use across a broad range of clinical and operational outcomes in DKA and provides an implementation framework for SUBQ insulin for mild-to-moderate DKA in the ED. We conducted a scoping review of PubMed from inception through February 2026 for adult studies evaluating SUBQ insulin for DKA. Two investigators independently screened studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Data were charted and synthesized across clinical, operational, and implementation outcomes. A total of 117 articles were identified and 13 included. Available evidence suggests SUBQ insulin may achieve similar time to DKA resolution, compared with IV insulin in select patients with uncomplicated DKA. SUBQ insulin offers potential operational benefits, including reduced intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, shorter ED length of stay, and improved resource optimization. Patient selection criteria, dosing and monitoring strategies, and implementation approaches are summarized. Limitations in the literature include small sample sizes, single-center designs, heterogeneous protocols, and the exclusion of several higher-risk patient populations. Evidence suggests SUBQ insulin pathways achieve similar clinical outcomes and may reduce ICU utilization and improve operational efficiency in select patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. Because most evidence originates from small, single-center cohorts, future studies should focus on larger, more generalizable populations.

articles.title: Fatal Opioid-Like Toxidrome Associated With a 7-Hydroxymitragynine Kratom Product.
articles.abstract: Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) use has increased in the United States, with the market shifting from traditional leaf preparations to concentrated products containing concentrated or chemically processed alkaloids such as 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG) and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. These formulations may deliver supraphysiologic opioid-receptor agonist doses with poorly characterized toxicity. A 42-year-old man was found dead at home after reportedly ingesting 3 tablets of a commercial "7-HMG" product and several beers. Postmortem examination revealed purge fluid at the mouth and nose, severe bilateral pulmonary edema, distended bladder, and no evidence of trauma or injection drug use. Quantitative analysis of the remaining tablet showed 29 mg 7-HMG and 0.58 mg mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, with minimal mitragynine. Postmortem blood contained 37.3 ng/mL 7-HMG and 76 ng/mL mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, whereas gabapentin and other medications were present at subtherapeutic concentrations. Compared with an estimated 1 to 4.5 mg 7-HMG in a typical high dose of dried kratom leaf powder, this ingestion delivered approximately 87 mg 7-HMG (19-fold to 87-fold greater 7-HMG exposure than a high-dose botanical leaf preparation). Given the high μ-opioid receptor activity of 7-HMG and its in vivo conversion to the even more potent opioid agonist mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, the postmortem findings are most consistent with a fatal opioid-like toxidrome associated with exposure to concentrated kratom alkaloids. This case illustrates the emerging risk posed by new kratom-branded products containing purified or chemically enriched alkaloids at doses far exceeding traditional preparations.

Associations Between Diagnostic Blood-Based Biomarkers and Neuroimaging Findings in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a prevalent and resource-intensive injury in the emergency department (ED). The blood-based biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have demonstrated diagnostic potential for acute structural brain injury. Our objective was to clinically validate a US Food and Drug Administration-approved plasma test to aid in the identification of intracranial injury in patients with mTBI presenting to the ED and assess its integration with existing protocols. This single-center validation study enrolled 104 adult patients with suspected mTBI undergoing head computed tomography (CT) for evaluation between October 2023 and June 2024 at a Level I trauma center. Peripheral blood draw was completed within 12 hours postinjury and processed at the hospital clinical laboratory. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for the test were calculated and compared with a standard clinical decision rule (Canadian Head CT Rule). ED length of stay and diagnostic turnaround times were examined. Within the cohort (n=104), 83 patients had elevated biomarker levels (GFAP >30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 >360 pg/mL), and 11 patients had intracranial injury identified on CT. The combination plasma test demonstrated high sensitivity (0.91 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.59 to 1.00]) but low specificity (0.22 [95% CI 0.14 to 0.31]) for predicting intracranial injury on CT with low positive predictive value (0.12 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.21]) and high negative predictive value (0.95 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.00]). These findings are consistent with prior studies (pooled sensitivity 0.97 [95% CI 0.95 to 0.98]; specificity 0.28 [95% CI 0.23 to 0.34]). False-positive cases (78%) were older than true-negative cases (median 72 years [interquartile range (IQR) 54 to 83] versus 58.5 years [IQR 38.25 to 66]). Median turnaround time for the GFAP/UCH-L1 test was 2 hours faster than head CT (1.09 hours [IQR 0.87 to 1.65] versus 3.28 hours [IQR 2.37 to 4.70]). Blood biomarkers for mTBI have potential as an initial rule-out tool for intracranial injury prior to obtaining CT imaging; however, large multicenter studies are needed to clarify its impact on ED resource utilization, length of stay, and acute and long-term costs and benefits to patients and health care systems.

articles.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.
articles.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes ("AI scribes") are purported to reduce emergency department (ED) documentation burden, but ED evidence is largely single-site, uncontrolled, or self-reported, with exposure inferred rather than measured. We evaluated AI scribe use among attending emergency physicians across a multisite network, with exposure and outcomes read directly from the electronic health record. Across 20 EDs (3 academic and 17 community), AI scribe use was flagged per note from the patient consent statement within the ED note. Analyses were restricted to attending physicians and, to isolate the physician's own documentation, excluded teaching encounters and attestation notes identified from standardized attestation text. Endpoints, computed over the mature-adoption window (December 2025 onward, when Epic audit-log data are retained), were active time in the note (primary), note length, note-start time, completion lag, and 72-hour ED return. Within-physician models (physician and calendar-month fixed effects, clustered by physician) compared each adopter's AI-scribed notes with their own unassisted notes, adjusting only for pre-exposure case mix. Among 275 attending physicians, 31% of encounters were AI-scribed. Physicians spent less active time in AI-scribed notes (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min-2.4 minutes after adjustment), started them about 15 minutes later (median 31 versus 17 minutes after first seeing the patient, and produced notes about 14% longer [median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters; within-physician +629 characters]). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1). Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

articles.title: Who's on Airway? Trainee Tracheal Intubation Frequency and Outcomes Within the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine (NEAR4PEM).
articles.abstract: We aimed to describe trainee performance and tracheal intubation outcomes in academic pediatric emergency departments. We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study of intubations performed between January 2021 and December 2023, using data from the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine. Eligible encounters included children who underwent intubation with the first-attempt proceduralist identified as an emergency medicine resident, a pediatric resident, or a pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellow. The primary outcome was first-attempt success. The secondary outcome was adverse airway outcomes, defined as desaturation or tracheal intubation-associated adverse events. We compared intubation outcomes across trainee groups. Over the 1,404 encounters during the study period, 642 (48%) were primary intubations performed on pediatric patients by an emergency medicine, pediatric or PEM trainee. A total of 343 (53%) first attempts were by emergency medicine residents, 254 (40%) by PEM fellows, and 45 (7%) by pediatric residents. The overall trainee first-attempt success rate was 471/642 (73%). First-attempt success by emergency medicine residents (75%) and PEM fellows (74%) were similar, and higher than first-attempt success by pediatric residents (58%). After accounting for potential confounders, there was no difference between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows in first-attempt success (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 to 1.28) or adverse airway outcome (aOR 1.4, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.18). In adjusted analysis, pediatric residents had a lower first-attempt success (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.82) and a higher adverse airway outcome (aOR 2.14, 95% CI 1.08 to 4.27) than emergency medicine residents. There was no difference in first-attempt success and adverse airway outcomes between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows. Pediatric residents have lower first-attempt success and higher adverse airway outcomes than emergency medicine residents.

An anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide augments whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock in a rodent polytrauma model.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Severe trauma induces a cytokine storm that is associated with impaired resuscitation and recovery. We investigated the impact of AQB-565, an anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide, as a novel treatment adjunct for whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock using a rat polytrauma shock model. Hemorrhagic shock with polytrauma was induced in 64 Sprague-Dawley rats. The rats were randomized to receive one of four intravenous treatments at 15 minutes posthemorrhage (T15): saline control, AQB-565, tranexamic acid (TXA), or combined AQB-565+ TXA. The rats were given autologous transfusion of shed whole blood at 60 minutes and as needed thereafter to achieve mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 60 mm Hg for up to 3 hours. Survival, hemodynamics, cytokine profiles, and hemorrhage volumes were compared between groups. There was a significant overall effect of treatment group on MAP (two-way rmANOVA p=0.02) that coincided with blood transfusion. MAP was significantly increased at T105 with AQB-565+TXA versus saline control (p=0.046). Inflammatory plasma cytokines, including interleukin-6, were significantly decreased with AQB-565 versus control groups (ANOVA p values ≤0.01). Seventeen (26.6%) rats died before 3 hours. There was a trend towards increased survival for treatments containing AQB-565 versus controls that was not statistically significant (Kaplan-Meier log rank p=0.06). A melanocortin pathway-activating polypeptide suppressed inflammation and improved hemodynamic response to whole blood transfusion in this hemorrhagic shock model.

Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

articles.title: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

Preliminary Exploration of the Hepatoprotective Effect of Nanocrystalline Curcumin Against Traumatic Hemorrhagic Shock-Induced Liver Injury in a Desert Dry-Heat Environment: A Network Pharmacology-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock (THS) under desert dry-heat conditions can exacerbate secondary liver injury, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic interventions. This study investigated the protective effects of nanocrystalline curcumin (NC-Cur) against THS-induced liver injury in a desert dry-heat environment and explored its potential molecular mechanisms. Network pharmacology, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were used to identify candidate targets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations examined curcumin-protein interactions. Forty male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control, model, solvent, or NC-Cur treatment groups (n = 10 each). The model, solvent, and treatment groups underwent traumatic hemorrhagic shock under desert dry-heat conditions. Hepatic injury was assessed by histopathology, serum aminotransferases, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and Western blotting. Network analysis identified 116 overlapping targets, with heat shock protein 90 alpha A1 (HSP90AA1), AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) prioritized as the core targets. Docking predicted favorable interactions with all three proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations supported stable binding between curcumin and HSP90AA1. Compared with untreated model rats, NC-Cur-treated rats showed attenuated hepatic histopathological injury, reduced alanine and aspartate aminotransferases, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, and malondialdehyde, and increased superoxide dismutase. Western blotting indicated reduced HSP90AA1 and increased phosphorylated AKT1 expression after NC-Cur treatment, with changes also observed in BCL-2 expression. These findings suggest that NC-Cur may alleviate liver injury associated with THS under desert dry-heat conditions in male rats, potentially involving HSP90AA1-AKT1-BCL-2-related signaling.

articles.title: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
articles.abstract: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay. Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis. Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness. This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity. Retrospective cohort study. Single academic medical center. None. Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation. We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation. A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
articles.abstract: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents. Prospective, multicenter, observational study. Thirteen ICUs in Poland. Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025. None. Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%). Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry.
authors: National Emergency Airway Registry for Children (NEAR4KIDS) investigators as a subgroup of Pediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators (PALISI)
articles.abstract: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs). Retrospective cohort study. Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs. Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs. Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry. TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%). TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.

articles.title: Non-Diagnostic Does Not Mean Non-Malignant: Outcomes and Predictors of Malignancy Following Nondiagnostic Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy.
Adherence to Non-Invasive Ventilation in a Provincial Cohort of Children.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) adherence is critical to its effectiveness, yet no standardized pediatric definition of "optimal" adherence exists, and population-level data are scarce. What are adherence patterns to NIV in children, and which factors are associated with adherence in a provincial longitudinal cohort? Canadian retrospective longitudinal cohort study linking records from the Ontario Ventilator Equipment Pool to health administrative databases. We identified children <18 years prescribed NIV with telemonitoring (2020 to 2022) and ≥1 month of data. The adherence definitions explored were the adult definition of ≥4 hours/day (primary) and measures of any daily use, daily NIV hours, and data missingness ("days not used" = 0 hours recorded; "days no data" = no signal). Mixed-effects regression models were used to explore adherence factors. We included 237 children (mean age 12.9 years; 61% male) with 3,685 person-months of NIV data (median 13 [IQR 8-24]). Across person-months, mean adherence by the ≥4-hours/day definition was 69.6%. Child-level monthly mean (SD) adherence was 59% (32%) by this definition, and 68% (26%) for any use. Mean (SD) daily use when used was 7.5 (3.2) hours. Monthly "days not used" and "no data" averaged 5.1 (6.4) and 4.4 (5.0) days, respectively. Greater adherence was associated with younger age (2-percentage-point decrease per year increase; 95% CI, 1-3), having ≥3 complex chronic conditions vs none (14 percentage-points higher; 95% CI, 3-26), and longer time prescribed NIV (2-percentage-point increase per year; 95% CI, 1-3). NIV adherence was moderate across definitions, with higher adherence among younger children, greater medical complexity, and those using therapy longer, highlighting the need for pediatric-specific adherence targets and home NIV support strategies.

articles.title: Comparison of delivery room wrist versus earlobe pulse oximetry in newborns: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition. Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications. Ninety-six neonates were randomized, with 48 in each group. Time from completion of sensor application to reliable signal was similar between ear and wrist groups (67.1±41.4 vs 74.5±48.2 seconds; mean difference -7.4 seconds; 95% CI -25.6 to 10.8; P=0.42). Sensor application time was shorter in ear group (mean difference -16.3 seconds; 95% CI -17.7 to -14.9; P<0.001), resulting in shorter time from birth to reliable signal (mean difference -28.8 seconds; 95% CI -53.9 to -3.7; P=0.02). Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group. Time to reliable signal acquisition after probe placement did not differ between the earlobe and wrist. Further studies using neonatal-specific ear probes are warranted.

articles.title: β-Blockade reprograms trauma-induced changes in bone marrow exosomal microRNAs.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Severe trauma produces sustained sympathetic activation that contributes to bone marrow dysfunction, impaired hematopoiesis, and persistent injury-associated anemia. Although β-adrenergic blockade improves bone marrow recovery after injury, the downstream mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol reprograms trauma-induced bone marrow extracellular vesicle (EV) microRNA (miRNA) expression toward restoration of hematopoietic homeostasis. Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized to naïve, polytrauma (PT), PT plus propranolol (PT+BB), PT with chronic restraint stress (PTRS), or PTRS plus propranolol (PTRS+BB) groups (n=6-8 per group). Propranolol (10 mg/kg intraperitoneally) was administered daily. On day 7, complete blood counts were obtained, and bone marrow-derived EV miRNAs were profiled using the NanoString nCounter platform. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using an absolute log2 fold change ≥1.5 and p<0.05. Predicted pathways were assessed using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, and miR-125b-5p was validated by quantitative PCR. PT altered 45 EV miRNAs compared with naïve animals, including suppression of miRNAs involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and erythropoiesis. Chronic restraint stress amplified this response, with 93 differentially expressed miRNAs following PTRS. Propranolol altered 12 miRNAs after PT and 43 after PTRS, increasing hematopoietic regulatory miRNAs, including miR-125b-5p, while suppressing several stress- and inflammation-associated miRNAs. Pathway analysis identified alterations in NOTCH, RUNX1, PTEN, thyroid receptor/retinoid X receptor, and histone modification signaling. Quantitative PCR confirmed a 2.4-fold increase in EV miR-125b-5p following propranolol in PTRS animals (p=0.018). Trauma and persistent adrenergic stress broadly remodel bone marrow EV miRNA signaling. β-Adrenergic blockade selectively reprograms these networks toward pathways associated with hematopoietic recovery, identifying EV miRNAs as potential mediators of posttraumatic bone marrow dysfunction. Not applicable-Animal research.

articles.title: The impact of presentations in scientific conferences: Publication and citation rates in trauma surgery.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Understanding the publication rates and citation patterns of conference abstracts is critical for program committees and investigators alike. However, the downstream scholarly outcome of conference abstracts remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that across contemporary US trauma-related scientific meetings, a substantial proportion of conference abstracts would not progress to peer-reviewed publications, and that publication rates and citation patterns would vary by presentation format and conference. We conducted a cross-sectional study of abstracts presented at four major US trauma surgery conferences from 2017 to 2019. We identified peer-reviewed manuscripts associated with conference abstracts via Google Scholar and PubMed. We collected presentation format, publishing journal, 2024 journal impact factor, and citation count. A cohort of directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts was also analyzed. Mixed-effects Poisson regression models assessed the association between presentation and citation counts, adjusting for publication timing. Of 1,157 abstracts, 762 (66%) were published as peer-reviewed manuscripts. Most manuscripts were published in the Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery (JTACS) (55%), with 5 in journals with a higher-impact factor than JTACS. On regression analysis, abstracts presented as oral presentations, and published in journals with an impact factor higher than JTACS, were associated with a greater number of citations. When comparing manuscripts presented as abstracts to directly submitted peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstract presentation was associated with 22% more citations (incidence rate ratio: 1.22; 95% CI [1.16-1.29]; p<0.001). This cross-sectional study of four trauma societies found that approximately a third of presented abstracts did not progress to peer-reviewed publication, with publication rates varying by conference and presentation format. Exploratory analyses found that among those published in JTACS, published manuscripts originating from presented abstracts demonstrated a modestly higher citation count compared with directly submitted manuscripts. Our findings highlight an opportunity to better understand how conference time and investigator effort translate into downstream scholarly output. Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level IV.

Diagnostic Contribution of Endobronchial Optical Coherence Tomography in the Multidisciplinary Diagnosis of Interstitial Lung Disease.
articles.abstract: Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB. How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC? Patients with low-confidence ILD diagnosis clinically referred for both TBLC with EGC were enrolled to undergo concurrent EB-OCT imaging. Each modality was interpreted independently by blinded pathologists. Separate MDD sessions were conducted at two independent sites, including one without prior EB-OCT experience. Fifteen patients were included (9 male; mean age: 70.6 years) with final diagnoses of UIP/IPF (n=5), secondary UIP (n=2), and various non-UIP ILDs (n=8) in agreement at both MDDs. EB-OCT provided diagnostic data that was in agreement with final MDD diagnosis for 100% of subjects (15/15), including in the 40% of subjects (6/15) where TBLC was non-diagnostic. In the subjects where TBLC yielded diagnostic data (60%, 9/15), EB-OCT diagnosis was in agreement. EB-OCT combined with TBLC/EGC increased diagnostic confidence and/or narrowed the differential diagnosis from baseline clinical/radiologic data review in all subjects, with replication across both independent MDDs. In this pilot study, we demonstrate EB-OCT is a safe, large-volume imaging method that detects microscopic features and patterns for ILD diagnosis, which increases diagnostic confidence in the context of MDD and complements TBLC and EGC. Future multicenter studies are needed to further validate these findings.

articles.title: Determinants of lung cancer screening follow-up care in community care settings: A qualitative multi-case study in the ACCELL trial.
articles.abstract: Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is <50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied. What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings? This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. We conducted rapid ethnographic assessments (REA) through virtual and in person site visits of LCS delivery in three community-based healthcare systems in Washington state. Additionally at the two future intervention sites, we conducted provider and patient interviews. Interview transcripts were analyzed using Rapid Group Analysis Process. All data were triangulated according to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework domains. Twenty-eight organizational leaders, providers, and staff participated in REA. Thirty-one patients and 15 providers from the future intervention sites participated in interviews. Determinants of LCS follow-up in the intervention domain included role of primary care, LCS complexity and care process standardization. In the inner setting domain (organization and clinic), screening prioritization, EHR use, radiology support, and context of wellness visits affected LCS. The main theme in the outer setting domain was the influence of social determinants of health on LCS. In the individuals domain, shared beliefs in LCS and LCS education and information sharing were key. In the process implementation domain, clinical champions and use of data and metrics were crucial. Integrated findings suggest determinants related to LCS complexity, care fragmentation, socioeconomic status and language, and limitations of PCPs could be overcome through more centralized approaches. However, increased use of EHR tools, increased education and standardizing LCS performance metrics may enable follow-up in decentralized settings. NCT06324110.

articles.title: Some nights stay with you.
Point-of-care ultrasound for confirming endotracheal tube placement in prehospital and critical care transport: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has demonstrated high pooled diagnostic accuracy for endotracheal tube (ETT) placement confirmation in adult Emergency Departments and Intensive Care Units,, but its translation to pre-hospital and Critical Care Transport (CCT) environments is unclear. We mapped the published evidence on POCUS-based ETT placement confirmation in transport, organized around six axes: clinical indication, transport modality, operator training, impact on management, technical barriers, and patient-oriented outcomes. Scoping review per the Joanna Briggs Institute 2020 framework, reported per PRISMA-ScR. Nine sources searched January 1st, 2015-May 12th, 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Europe PMC, Consensus.app, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and forward-citation tracking. Dual independent screening and charting were performed in Covidence with built-in conflict adjudication. From 2447 unique records, 51 met final inclusion. One primary study evaluated diagnostic performance in adult patients in an out-of-hospital setting. The remaining 50 records comprised contextual primary studies and secondary evidence, including cadaver and simulation studies, training evaluations, feasibility implementations, and reviews. Distribution by modality was skewed toward ground emergency medical services (EMS); rotor-wing helicopter EMS (HEMS) evidence was predominantly training-based; fixed-wing evidence was essentially absent. Operator profiles in transport-relevant studies were predominantly paramedic, flight medic, or flight nurse, mismatched against the physician-dominant pooled in-hospital meta-analytic estimates. No included study measured patient-oriented outcomes. Evidence supporting POCUS-based ETT confirmation in pre-hospital and critical care transport remains limited. Most studies addressed training, simulation, feasibility, or implementation rather than diagnostic performance in transported patients, and none demonstrated an effect on patient-oriented outcomes. Transport-specific prospective studies are needed before hospital-derived diagnostic-accuracy estimates can be generalized to transport practice.

articles.title: Naxos disease: current insights from early clinical observations to genetics and precision medicine.
articles.abstract: Naxos disease is the prototype of the Naxos disease cardiocutaneous spectrum, a group of inherited desmosomal disorders characterised by distinctive hair and skin abnormalities that precede the development of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM). Since its original clinical description in 1986 and the subsequent identification of the first ACM-causing gene (JUP), Naxos disease has provided fundamental insights into the pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of inherited desmosomal cardiomyopathies. This review provides current insights into the evolving clinical spectrum, encompassing the characteristic cutaneous signature, early electrical abnormalities, progressive structural myocardial remodelling, inflammatory ("hot-phase") episodes, ventricular arrhythmias and heart failure. We discuss the expanding genotype-phenotype relationships involving JUP, DSP and DSC2, highlighting how distinct genetic substrates influence ventricular involvement, disease severity and clinical outcomes while sharing common desmosomal mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on early clinical recognition, multimodality imaging, genetic diagnosis, risk stratification and lifelong multidisciplinary management. Finally, we discuss the emerging role of international collaborative registries, including NAXCARE, in generating prospective real-world evidence to refine genotype-informed surveillance, improve risk prediction and support precision medicine. Nearly four decades after its original description, Naxos disease has evolved from a rare inherited syndrome into the prototype of desmosomal cardiomyopathy, demonstrating how careful clinical observation can drive molecular discovery, precision medicine and improved patient care.

articles.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO. Laboratory investigation. University Hospital. Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10). Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO. We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects. Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

Scientific Output in Septic Shock According to Country Income and Gender: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract: We aimed to assess trends in septic shock publications by country income and author gender. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for articles indexed with "septic shock" between January 2014 and December 2024. All peer-reviewed publication types were eligible. Conference abstracts and non-peer-reviewed material were excluded. Bibliographic data, first and last author affiliations, country income level (World Bank classification: low- and middle-income countries [LMICs] and high-income countries [HICs]), and journal prestige (SCImago Journal Rank [SJR]) were extracted. Author gender was inferred using the NamSor application programming interface (API). Of 10,352 eligible publications, LMIC-affiliated first authors increased over time (+2.13% per year; 95% CI, +1.66 to +2.61; p < 0.001) from 18% in 2014 to 37% in 2024. Women represented 35.6% of first authors and 25.0% of last authors (with around 20% of authors not classifiable by the NamSor API), with higher proportions in LMICs than HICs (p < 0.001) for both first authors (44.5% vs. 32.5%) and last authors (35.2% vs. 21.5%). Gender concordance was more frequent, with female first authors more often paired with female last authors than male first authors (31.7% vs. 21.1%). Cross-income collaborations, especially involving LMIC last authors, remained rare. Articles led by men in HICs were more often published in higher-SJR journals compared with those led by women (p < 0.001), whereas no gender differences were observed among LMIC-affiliated authors. Despite encouraging growth in LMIC contributions and female representation, major inequities persist. Strengthening equitable collaborations and supporting underrepresented groups would broaden participation and enhance the global applicability in critical care research.

articles.title: Cluster Versus Individual Randomization in Prehospital, Emergency and Critical Care Trials: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase. We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT. Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes. Using absolute ln(odds ratio [OR]) for mortality and absolute Hedges' g for the secondary outcome, mean differences (MDs) in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs were analyzed using mixed regression models, presented with 95% CIs. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT). We included 65 meta-analyses in quantitative analyses, encompassing 212 randomized clinical trials (39 cRCTs and 173 iRCTs) and 315,276 patients. No statistically significant difference in absolute ln(OR) for mortality between cRCTs and iRCTs was found (MD, -0.110; 95% CI, -0.093 to 0.313). For length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, a significant difference in absolute Hedges' g was found (MD, -0.202; 95% CI, -0.392 to -0.012). A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.

articles.title: Furosemide Stress Test in Adults and Children With Acute Kidney Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic utility of the furosemide stress test (FST) for acute kidney injury (AKI) management in critically ill adults and children. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 3, 2026. Studies evaluating the standardized FST protocol in critically ill adults or children with AKI were eligible. Outcomes included AKI stage 3 progression (Q1), kidney replacement therapy (KRT) initiation (Q2), short-term mortality (Q3), successful KRT liberation (Q4), and FST-guided vs. standard KRT initiation in randomized trials (Q5). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 and Risk of Bias 2. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Twenty studies (n = 1979; 11 countries; 2013-2025) were included. For AKI progression (nine studies; n = 501), pooled sensitivity was 0.69 and specificity was 0.88 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.89; GRADE: low). For KRT initiation (nine studies; n = 952), sensitivity was 0.81 and specificity was 0.75 (AUC, 0.79; GRADE: very low). For mortality (six studies; n = 487), sensitivity was 0.56 and specificity was 0.76 (AUC, 0.75; GRADE: very low). For KRT liberation (three studies; n = 177), sensitivity was 0.81 and specificity was 0.87 (AUC, 0.89; GRADE: low for sensitivity, very low for specificity). The effect of FST-guided early KRT initiation on short-term mortality was uncertain (pooled risk ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.79-1.27; two randomized controlled trials, n = 212; GRADE: very low). Pediatric analyses yielded AUC values of 0.81 and 0.63 for KRT initiation and mortality, respectively. Based on low to very low certainty evidence, the FST may support risk stratification for AKI progression and KRT liberation in critically ill adults. Its impact on mortality when guiding early KRT initiation remains uncertain. As a low-cost bedside test, the FST can be a useful tool in resource-limited settings where novel biomarkers are inaccessible.

Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
authors: and the Cooperative Antimicrobial Therapy of Septic Shock (CATSS) Database Research Group
articles.abstract: To determine the effect of delays in initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy from the initial onset of persistent hypotension to the outcome of Candida septic shock. Retrospective cohort study. A total of 32 academic and community hospitals in Canada, the United States, and Saudi Arabia (July 1989 to June 2018). A total of 850 adult patients with culture-positive Candida septic shock. None. Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. A strong relationship was observed between the delay in initiation of pathogen-appropriate antifungal (PAA) therapy and hospital survival. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. In a multivariate analysis, which included the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and epidemiologic/therapeutic variables, the time to initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy emerged as the single strongest predictor of outcome. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that the adverse effects of delayed antifungal treatment were consistent across various subgroups, including different types of infections, pathogens, and antifungal drug classes. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset. Administration of PAAs within the first hours of documented hypotension significantly improved hospital survival. Less than 20% of patients received appropriate antifungals within 6 hours of documented hypotension.

Music Therapy During Weaning From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: The study examined the effect of daily music therapy on weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in the ICU, with a primary focus on weaning duration. Secondary agitation, sedation, and analgesia doses, pain, delirium, and perceived stress after 90 days were assessed. Additionally, total IMV and ICU stay durations and tracheostomy rates were studied. Physiologic parameters were assessed in the music therapy group (MG). The study also aimed to promote the humanization of critical care through a biopsychosocial and creative music therapy approach. Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally. Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours. MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation. No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy. Music therapy may serve as a nonpharmacological complementary adjunct during weaning by reducing agitation, sedation, and tracheostomy rate. It may potentially decrease perceived stress and IMV and ICU stay durations. Further research is warranted.

Modifiers of the effectiveness of point-of-care troponin testing and determinants of concordance between diagnostic pathway recommendations and disposition in patients with chest pain: a post hoc analysis of a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: While point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) testing has the potential to reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS), evidence of real world effectiveness is lacking. Our objective was to examine factors that influence the real world effectiveness of POC hs-cTn-based accelerated diagnostic protocols (ADPs) in reducing ED LOS. This is a post hoc analysis from the “Aiming towards evidence-based interpretation of cardiac biomarkers in patients presenting with chest pain using POC testing” (WESTCOR-POC) study which included 1494 consecutive patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome presenting to the ED at a moderately sized hospital in Norway. Patients were randomised to receive hs-cTn measurements at admission and after 1 hour either by POC or central laboratory testing. This post hoc analysis examines factors affecting the effectiveness of a POC-based ADP and predictors of non-ADP-concordant disposition. Both outcomes were assessed using regression models, with significance level set at p<0.05. Overall, 36.1% of patients met the ADPs’ early discharge criteria, of which 66% were discharged. In effect-modification analyses, the effect of POC testing on ED LOS differed by concordance with ADP recommendations (interaction p=0.011), with a reduction among patients with ADP-concordant disposition (−14 min 95% CI −26 to −3), but no corresponding reduction among patients with discordant disposition (13.5 min, 95% CI −4.5 to 31.4). Factors predicting hospital admission despite ADP-recommended discharge were: age >60 years (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.4 to 3.7, p=0.001), high triage category (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.2 to 3.0, p=0.003) and suspected serious differential diagnosis (OR 5.9, 95% 3.5 to 9.9, p<0.001). Our findings highlight the need for implementation strategies that support ADP concordant disposition decisions and ensure appropriate patient selection to realise the efficiency potential of POC hs-cTn testing in the ED.

articles.title: Accuracy of deep learning in quantifying epicardial adipose tissue: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is significantly associated with cardiovascular disease and poor prognosis. Deep learning (DL) models have been explored for automatic EAT segmentation, but systematic evidence verifying their effectiveness is currently lacking. We conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and quantification, aiming to support the development of automated tools. We searched the Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore through February 20, 2026. Studies reporting DL-based quantitative EAT segmentation were included. Quality was assessed with QUADAS-2. The Dice similarity coefficient (Dice), correlation coefficient (R), and Bland-Altman bias were used to evaluate segmentation efficacy, the correlation between automated segmentation and reference standards, and consistency, respectively. A random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method pooled these measures. Thirty eligible studies were included, covering five image types. For non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), the pooled Dice was 0.888 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.853-0.924), and the pooled R reached 0.973 (95%CI: 0.958-0.982). The contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) subgroup performed best, yielding a Dice of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.881-0.939) and an R of 0.989 (95% CI: 0.976-0.995). This meta-analysis quantifies the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and volume quantification. The findings indicate that DL achieves robust accuracy on both NCCT and CECT images. However, given that most current studies rely on internal validation, future work should prioritize large-scale, multicenter external validation to support the translation of these promising DL tools into robust clinical diagnostic systems.

articles.title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.
articles.abstract: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

articles.title: Association between the site of emergency care and patient-centered outcomes in patients with cancer: rationale and design of the French COVER cohort.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Patients living with cancer now account for a substantial and growing share of emergency department (ED) visits and carry a high burden of hospitalization and in-hospital death. Their acute presentations are frequently multifactorial - driven by disease progression, treatment toxicity, immunosuppression, or the decompensation of comorbid conditions. They may present with higher rates of complications because of novel therapies, such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and cellular therapies, whose emergency manifestations remain unfamiliar to many emergency physicians. Despite this growing importance, the unscheduled care of patients with cancer has received comparatively little dedicated research. How these patients are managed in the ED, how often the emergency physician can access the oncology medical record and goals of care, how the acute complications of new anticancer therapies present, and how a background of cancer should modify the diagnostic approach to everyday emergencies remain poorly characterized. To address these gaps, the Cohort of Onco-hematologic patients visiting the Emergency depaRtment was designed as a prospective, multicenter French cohort of consecutive adults with active cancer or in remission for less than 1 year, presenting to the ED for any reason. Enrollment took place across a national network of 76 EDs for two 1-week periods (summer 2025 and winter 2025-2026), with follow-up to 90 days, yielding a large sample of patients designed as a platform for multiple analyses. The primary aim of Cohort of Onco-hematologic patients visiting the Emergency depaRtment is to determine whether being managed in an ED located within the patient's own cancer referral center, rather than any other hospital, is associated with improvement in morbidity and mortality, captured by the number of days alive and out of hospital at 30 days. Beyond this primary aim, the cohort will support a broad research program on the place of the ED in the cancer care pathway, from patient profiling and pathway description to the emergency toxicities of anticancer drugs and the cancer-specific features of common presentations.

articles.title: Epidemiology, clinical profile, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending at Spanish emergency departments (EDEN-56 study).
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Older adults with active cancer are increasing, clinically complex emergency department (ED) population, but large multicenter European data are limited. To describe the epidemiology, baseline characteristics, diagnoses, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending Spanish EDs, and assess whether associations between active cancer and short-term outcomes varied with age and sex. Secondary analysis of the Emergency Department and Elder Needs retrospective multicenter registry, including all patients aged greater than or equal to 65 years attending 52 Spanish EDs during 1-7 April 2019. Patients with and without active cancer were compared. Annualized incidence was extrapolated overall, by sex, and by age. Age-related patterns were modeled using restricted cubic splines. ED length of stay, hospitalization, length of hospitalization, and index-episode death. Age-by-cancer and age-by-sex interactions were assessed in unadjusted and multivariable models. Among 25 557 older ED patients, 4701 (18.4%) had active cancer. The estimated annualized incidence of ED presentations was 10 885 per 100 000 inhabitants aged greater than or equal to 65 years [95% confidence interval (CI): 10 576-11 200], higher in men (annualized rate ratio: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.70-1.91) and in the mid-to-late 80s. Patients with cancer had more severe comorbidity (58.9 vs. 12.9%), polypharmacy (26.6 vs. 21.3%), and walking handicaps (31.5 vs. 28.2%). Malignancy accounted for only 7.7% of ED diagnoses in the cancer group; infections, heart failure, and respiratory conditions were frequent. Active cancer was associated with longer median ED stay (4.0 vs. 3.3 h; adjusted difference: 0.3, 95% CI: 0.1-0.4), higher hospitalization [32.5 vs. 24.0%; adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.34, 95% CI: 1.25-1.44], longer median hospitalization (7.5 vs. 6.9 days; adjusted difference: 0.5, 0.1-0.9), and higher index-episode mortality (5.5 vs. 2.5%; adjusted OR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.81-2.50). Age significantly modified ED length of stay, hospitalization, and mortality, with significantly different age-related changes between patients with and without cancer. Among patients with cancer, age-related trajectories did not significantly differ by sex. Active cancer is common among older ED patients and associated with substantial resource use and worse short-term outcomes. These associations vary with age, supporting multidimensional assessment beyond chronological age or cancer status alone.
